Kuvitus: kaupungin katu kesäpäivänä. Val: Illustration: a city street on a summer day. A white ambulance with a blue emergency light on its roof drives along the street from left to right. The sound of the siren spreads out as arcs, close together in front of the ambulance and far apart behind it. On the right-hand pavement next to a pedestrian crossing stands a pedestrian, whom the ambulance is just about to pass. In the background are houses and a birch tree.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa. Ylhäällä va: Schematic figure, not to scale. At the top left is a loudspeaker with air in a tube in front of it. The air particles are drawn as blue dots, in places close together and in places far apart: the dense places are compressions and the sparse ones rarefactions. The particles vibrate back and forth along the direction in which the wave travels, shown by a small double-headed arrow, and the wave travels to the right, shown by a blue arrow. Below is the pressure at the same moment as a function of position: the curve varies on both sides of the normal air pressure p0, and its peaks are at the compressions. The distance between two neighbouring compressions is the wavelength lambda.
Kaavakuva: taajuusasteikko logaritmisena: Schematic figure: a logarithmic frequency scale from one hertz to ten million hertz, each tenfold increase the same length. Frequencies below 20 hertz are infrasound, from 20 hertz to 20 kilohertz is the human range of hearing and frequencies above 20 kilohertz are ultrasound. Above the scale are marked examples: an earthquake at about one hertz, the low sounds of elephants at about 15 hertz, speech from a few hundred hertz to a few kilohertz, the echolocation of a bat at about 50 kilohertz and ultrasound imaging at about three megahertz.
Kaavakuva kahdesta äänestä, joilla on sa: Schematic figure of two sounds with the same fundamental frequency of 220 hertz. At the top a tuning fork, at the bottom a guitar. On the left is pressure as a function of time: the curve of the tuning fork is a sine wave, the curve of the guitar is more complicated, but the period T of both curves is the same. On the right is the spectrum, that is, the FFT graph, of each sound: the tuning fork has one peak at 220 hertz, the guitar has peaks at 220, 440, 660, 880 and 1100 hertz, that is, at multiples of the fundamental frequency, and the peaks get smaller as the frequency increases.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: kaksi ääntä: Schematic figure, not to scale: two sounds whose frequencies f1 and f2 differ slightly, and their sum as a function of time. At the top an orange wave and below it a purple wave that has two more vibrations during the picture. At the bottom is the blue sum wave: its amplitude alternately grows and shrinks following the envelope drawn with a dashed line. Where the waves are in phase the sum is strong, and where they are in opposite phase the sum is almost zero. The time between two successive strong places is the period of the beats T h.
Kaavakuva ylhäältä katsottuna, kaksi til: Schematic figure seen from above, two situations one below the other. At the top the source moves to the right at 0.4 times the speed of sound, shown by a blue velocity arrow. The wavefronts are circles that have started from earlier positions of the source, so they are close together in front of the source and far apart behind it. In the direction of listener A on the right the wavelength lambda A is short, and in the direction of listener B on the left the wavelength lambda B is long. At the bottom the source is at rest and the wavefronts are concentric circles at equal intervals. The listener moves to the left towards the source, shown by a blue velocity arrow; the wavelength lambda is the same in all directions.
Kuvaaja: äänen FFT-spektri. Vaaka-akseli: Graph: the FFT spectrum of a sound. On the horizontal axis the frequency f in hertz from zero to 1200 hertz, with grid lines every one hundred hertz and numbers every two hundred hertz. On the vertical axis the relative height of the peak from zero to one. The spectrum has five narrow peaks at 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1000 hertz. The heights of the peaks are about 0.6, 1.0, 0.45, 0.3 and 0.15; the highest peak is at 400 hertz.
Kuvaaja: kahden yhtä aikaa soivan äänira: Graph: the combined sound of two tuning forks sounding at the same time, measured with a microphone, pressure as a function of time from zero to one second. On the time axis there are grid lines every 0.1 seconds and numbers every 0.2 seconds. The vibration is so dense that it appears as a filled blue area. The width of the area varies: it is greatest at the moments 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.00 seconds and narrows almost to zero halfway between them.
